summary: Intermittent AWS->GCP credential propagation failures blocking ephemeral dev environments
description:
Issue summary:
Ephemeral dev environments provisioned by the internal provisioner intermittently fail to receive cross-cloud credentials (AWS->GCP) during onboarding. Errors surface as STS AssumeRole/TokenExchange failures and IAM "permission denied" messages in the credential-broker logs. This blocks engineers from debugging dedicated/double-cloud test jobs and delays feature testing.

Impact:
- ~10% of ephemeral environment provisions in us-east and us-west fail to complete within the 10m onboarding window.
- Affected users cannot run integrated multi-cloud debug jobs.
- Workaround requires manual re-run of the provisioner or hand syncing of temporary bindings.

Environment:
- prod provisioner cluster (k8s: provisioner-prod-3) in us-east, fallback in us-west.
- credential-broker v1.9.2, sts-exchange v0.7.1.
- GCP projects: redwood-dev-{team}, AWS accounts: rw-infra-dev, rw-dedicated-demo.

Observed behavior:
- Provision request succeeds until credential exchange step. Brokering logs show transient 403/401 errors and "audience mismatch" in token exchange.

Expected behavior:
- Provisioner should obtain signed temporary credentials from AWS and exchange them with GCP broker reliably within retries, or fail fast with actionable error for the user.

Additional context:
- This looks different from prior long-running org-policy denies because the errors are intermittent and correlate with high SCIM sync activity windows and short-lived session timings.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Trigger ephemeral environment build for a developer repo that requires AWS->GCP cross-account access (use provisioner-prod-3).
2) Observe logs from provisioner and credential-broker during the exchange phase (timestamps between CR create and CR ready).
3) If failure occurs, check broker logs and cloud audit logs for STS errors and audience/session tags.
4) Repeat until intermittent failure reproduces (we observed ~1 in 10).
logs:
credential-broker ERROR 2026-03-10T14:22:08Z token_exchange failed: 403 PermissionDenied: Token audience mismatch (expected: projects/12345/serviceAccounts/exchange, got: projects/67890/serviceAccounts/exchange-client)
sts-exchange WARN 2026-03-10T14:22:08Z assumeRole returned 200 but session tags truncated: sessionName truncated from 'provisioner-prod-3-builder-very-long-name' to 'provisioner-prod-3-builder'
aws-iam DEBUG 2026-03-10T14:22:07Z AssumeRole response: Arn: arn:aws:sts::111222333444:assumed-role/provisioner-role/provision-session
cloud-audit ERROR 2026-03-10T14:22:08Z deny: request denied by org policy 'require-sso-tag'
investigation_notes:
Timeline and checks performed:
- Reproduced failure in staging with increased logging, correlated failed exchanges to SCIM group sync spikes (timestamps align with our SCIM connector logs).
- Verified that the provisioner retries the exchange 3x with exponential backoff; failures happen across all retries.
- Confirmed session tag truncation in a subset of AssumeRole calls (session name >64 chars) which leads downstream role binding evaluation to fail due to tag mismatch.
- Observed TTL mismatch between our permission-syncer and cloud provider caches (permission-syncer writes take ~45s to propagate, cloud IAM enforcement checks within 10-20s window).
- Hypothesis A: Race between permission sync propagation and token exchange timing causing transient Deny.
- Hypothesis B: STS session name truncation causes tag-based allowlist checks to not match the expected pattern.
- Evidence: Failed exchanges show both "audience mismatch" and tag-name mismatch in separate traces; not all failures show both.
- Runbook referenced: Cloud Access Propagation Runbook (linked).
resolution:
Immediate mitigations applied:
1) Short-term: Added a 60s deterministic delay before final token exchange in provisioner to allow permission-syncer propagation. Deployed as hotfix provisioner v1.9.3-hotfix. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/provisioner/pull/428
2) Fixed session name handling in sts-exchange to truncate predictably and include a stable hash suffix to avoid collisions (deployed v0.7.2).
3) Added monitoring alert on credential-broker for >3 token_exchange failures within 5m for a single provisioner instance.

Follow-ups (owner assigned):
- Create a proper eventual-consistency design: change permission-syncer to SQS-based handshake so provisioner receives a propagation confirmation event rather than relying on time delays. (ENG-PI: provisioner-sync-reliability, owner: Diego Martinez, due: 2026-04-02)
- Audit session-name limits across services and enforce stable naming in provisioning templates. (owner: SRE team, due: 2026-03-19)
- Add end-to-end test that simulates SCIM spikes to catch regressions. (owner: QA, due: 2026-03-26)
